ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached diagram shows a circle with Z as the center, W on the left side of the circle, U on the right side, and segment WU passes through Z, being a horizontal diameter. V is at the upper-left position of the circle, Y is at the lower-right position of the circle, and segment VY passes through Z, being an oblique diameter. There is also a radius from Z pointing to point X on the circumference at the lower left. In the diagram, ray ZU is located within the semicircle between opposite rays ZV and ZY, and V is located on the upper semicircle from W to U. Reasoning: Because VY is a diameter, ZV and ZY are opposite rays, forming 180°. In the diagram, ray ZU is between them, therefore ∠VZU + ∠UZY = 180°. Substitute the known values: 4x + (2x + 24) = 180, obtaining 6x + 24 = 180, so 6x = 156, x = 26. Thus m∠VZU = 4x = 104°. Also because WU is a diameter, ∠WZU = 180°. In the diagram, V is between W and U on the upper semicircle, therefore ∠WZV + ∠VZU = 180°, so ∠WZV = 180° - 104° = 76°. Arc WV is the minor arc intercepted by central angle ∠WZV, therefore m arc WV = 76.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a circle centered at Z with WU a horizontal diameter and VY a slanted diameter; V, U, Y are consecutive around the right/top side, and W and V bound the requested minor arc. From the text, use m∠VZU=4x, m∠UZY=2x+24, and VY is a diameter. Since ZV and ZY are opposite rays and ray ZU lies between them in the image, ∠VZU+∠UZY=180°, so 4x+(2x+24)=180 and x=26. Then ∠VZU=104°. Since WU is a diameter and V lies on the upper semicircle between W and U, ∠WZV+∠VZU=180°, giving ∠WZV=76°. Convert the central angle to the minor arc measure: m arc WV=76.
